chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Dinawari, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Salih ibn Uqba, who said:

I entered upon Jamil ibn Darraj, and in front of him was a tray with a Gassanite dish from which he was eating. He said, 'Come near and eat.' I said, 'I am fasting.' So he left me until he had finished it, and only a little remained. Then he insisted upon me, 'Will you not break your fast?' I said to him, 'Why did you not do this earlier?' He said, 'I wanted to discipline you with that.' Then he said, 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Whoever a believing man visits while he is fasting, and asks him to eat, and he does not inform him of his fasting so as to favor him with his breaking of the fast, Allah, Majestic is His Praise, will write for him for that day the fasting of a year.'

key_terms.خِوَانٌ: A tray or platter for food
key_terms.غَسَّانِيَّةٌ: A type of dish or bread from Gassan

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for a host who offers food to a fasting guest without telling them they are fasting?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the nuanced etiquette of hospitality in Shia tradition, where a host may intentionally withhold information about a guest's fast to prevent the guest from breaking it out of politeness, thereby earning the reward of a year's fasting. The narrative highlights the balance between *adab* (etiquette) and *ihsan* (excellence in conduct), emphasizing that the host's intention to benefit the guest spiritually is key to this virtue. It serves as a practical guide for social interactions during Ramadan, prioritizing the guest's comfort and spiritual gain over rigid adherence to fasting protocols.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Deynawry, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Salih Bin Uqba who said,

‘I went over to Jameel Bin Darraj and in front of him was a meal, eating eagerly from it. So he said, ‘Approach and eat’. So I said, ‘I am Fasting’. So he neglected me until when he had eaten it, and there did not remain from it except for a little, he insisted upon me, ‘Will you not break?’ So I said to him, ‘Why did you not insist before this time?’ So he said, ‘I wanted to educate you with that’. Then he said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Whichever Believing man goes over to his brother and he is Fasting, so he asks him to eat, and he does not inform him of his Fasting to favour upon him with his breaking, Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Majestic is His<sup>azwj</sup> Praise, would Write for that day for him, the Fasts of a year’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Daynawariy from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Salih ibn ‘Uqbah who has said the following:

“Once I visited Jamil ibn Darraj while he was at a beautiful table having food. He said, ‘Come and join us for food.’ I said, ‘I am fasting.’ He continued eating until very little food remained. He then insisted that I discontinue my fast. I said, ‘Why did you not insist before?’ He said, ‘I wanted to discipline you.’ He then said, ‘I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say the following. “If a fasting person visits his brother (in belief), who offers him food, and he accepts the offer without telling him about his fast, in order not to show that he is doing him a favor by accepting his offering food, Allah, majestic is whose mention, counts his fast as one year’s fasting.’””
